_metadata.note: These are learning guides and interview models, not authoritative snapshots of each company's current internal production architecture. Publicly documented patterns are used where available; implementation details can change.

scenarios.title: Netflix Video Streaming
learningObjectives: Understand why control-plane APIs and video delivery paths should be separated
Learn adaptive-bitrate streaming and edge caching
Reason about multi-region resilience for a global media platform

keyDecisions.decision: Why deliver video through edge caches instead of application servers
keyDecisions.reason: Video segments are large and repeatedly requested. ISP-local and edge caches reduce origin load, transit distance, and buffering risk.

keyDecisions.decision: Why store multiple encoded renditions of the same title
keyDecisions.reason: Clients can switch bitrate as network conditions change rather than waiting for a single oversized stream.

keyDecisions.decision: Why isolate playback metadata from playable media bytes
keyDecisions.reason: Metadata APIs need personalization and rapid iteration; media delivery needs efficient cacheable transfer.

interestingFacts: Netflix Open Connect localizes traffic through embedded appliances and interconnection with ISPs.
Netflix clients monitor network conditions and dynamically choose bitrate and CDN server during playback.
Treat this guide as a learning model: production internals evolve continuously.
scenarios.commonInterviewQuestion: How would you design a global streaming platform that starts playback quickly and degrades gracefully during regional or CDN failures?

scenarios.title: Uber Ride-Hailing Dispatch
learningObjectives: Model real-time driver location updates
Design a nearby-driver search path with bounded latency
Handle trip state, payments, and notifications as separate reliability domains

keyDecisions.decision: Why separate the high-volume location stream from the transactional trip database
keyDecisions.reason: Location updates are frequent, ephemeral, and geo-indexed; trip state needs durable state transitions and auditability.

keyDecisions.decision: Why partition by geography
keyDecisions.reason: Most matching queries are local. Geographic partitioning limits fan-out and lets overloaded cities scale independently.

keyDecisions.decision: Why use events after trip-state changes
keyDecisions.reason: Notifications, analytics, pricing, and fraud systems can react asynchronously without delaying the core transition.

interestingFacts: A dispatch platform must distinguish current position from durable trip history.
Driver matching is a latency-sensitive approximation problem, not only a database lookup.
Idempotent state transitions matter because mobile networks retry requests.
scenarios.commonInterviewQuestion: Design Uber's driver-matching system for a stadium exit where demand increases sharply within one small area.

scenarios.title: WhatsApp Messaging
learningObjectives: Design durable message handoff for intermittently connected clients
Reason about ordering, delivery receipts, and idempotency
Separate message transport from media storage

keyDecisions.decision: Why assign conversation-aware routing or sequence metadata
keyDecisions.reason: Users expect messages in a chat to appear in a sensible order even when retries and reconnects occur.

keyDecisions.decision: Why store media in object storage and send references
keyDecisions.reason: Large media files should not block the low-latency text-message path.

keyDecisions.decision: Why support offline delivery queues
keyDecisions.reason: Recipients may be disconnected for hours; durable handoff is different from a live WebSocket connection.

interestingFacts: Messaging delivery semantics are usually discussed as accepted, delivered, and read rather than one vague 'sent' state.
End-to-end encryption changes what servers can inspect and search.
Presence updates should be treated as lossy and lower priority than durable messages.
scenarios.commonInterviewQuestion: How would you design one-to-one and group messaging with offline delivery, ordering, and read receipts?

scenarios.title: Twitter/X Home Timeline
learningObjectives: Compare fan-out-on-write and fan-out-on-read
Design a timeline cache for high read volume
Handle celebrity accounts and ranking as special cases

keyDecisions.decision: Why precompute timelines for many ordinary users
keyDecisions.reason: Reading the home feed becomes a fast cache lookup instead of merging thousands of accounts on every refresh.

keyDecisions.decision: Why avoid blindly fan-out-writing celebrity posts to every follower
keyDecisions.reason: A single post can trigger excessive writes. A hybrid approach merges high-fan-out authors at read time.

keyDecisions.decision: Why keep ranking separate from raw post storage
keyDecisions.reason: Ranking features and experiments evolve faster than the durable post model.

interestingFacts: Timeline design is a workload trade-off between write amplification and read latency.
A hybrid model is often stronger than choosing only push or pull.
Cache invalidation and backfill behavior are core design questions.
scenarios.commonInterviewQuestion: Design a home timeline that remains fast when an account with hundreds of millions of followers posts.

scenarios.title: Amazon E-Commerce Platform
learningObjectives: Separate catalog browsing from checkout correctness
Design inventory and order workflows using explicit state transitions
Use asynchronous processing without double-charging customers

keyDecisions.decision: Why use different stores for product search and order truth
keyDecisions.reason: Catalog search needs denormalized retrieval and filtering; orders need transactional correctness and auditability.

keyDecisions.decision: Why reserve inventory rather than decrementing casually
keyDecisions.reason: Checkout spans time and services. Reservations make expiry and compensation explicit.

keyDecisions.decision: Why make payment requests idempotent
keyDecisions.reason: Retries are unavoidable; a stable idempotency key prevents duplicate charges.

interestingFacts: Commerce systems mix read-heavy catalog traffic with correctness-sensitive checkout workflows.
A cart is not an order and should not be treated as durable inventory ownership.
Cell-based isolation can limit the blast radius of failures in very large platforms.
scenarios.commonInterviewQuestion: How would you design flash-sale checkout without overselling inventory or overwhelming the database?

scenarios.title: Airbnb Booking Marketplace
learningObjectives: Model availability calendars and search indexes
Prevent double booking under concurrency
Coordinate payment, reservation, and notification workflows

keyDecisions.decision: Why maintain a search index separate from booking truth
keyDecisions.reason: Search needs geo, filters, price ranges, and ranking. The reservation database must remain authoritative.

keyDecisions.decision: Why lock or atomically reserve a listing-date range during checkout
keyDecisions.reason: Two guests may attempt the same dates simultaneously; the system needs a clear winner.

keyDecisions.decision: Why recompute price at booking confirmation
keyDecisions.reason: Fees, rules, and availability may have changed since the search result was generated.

interestingFacts: Marketplace search results are snapshots, not guarantees.
Booking workflows benefit from saga-style compensation when payment or confirmation fails.
Fraud and trust signals influence both search and checkout paths.
scenarios.commonInterviewQuestion: Design Airbnb booking so two users cannot confirm the same property for overlapping dates.

scenarios.title: Stripe Payment Processing
learningObjectives: Design idempotent payment APIs
Separate synchronous authorization from asynchronous settlement events
Build auditability and webhook reliability

keyDecisions.decision: Why require idempotency keys for payment creation
keyDecisions.reason: Clients retry after timeouts; duplicate network requests must not create duplicate financial operations.

keyDecisions.decision: Why use a ledger-like append history
keyDecisions.reason: Balances and disputes require traceability. Mutating only the latest state hides how the system arrived there.

keyDecisions.decision: Why retry webhooks with signatures
keyDecisions.reason: Merchant endpoints fail temporarily; retries plus verification provide reliable and secure notification.

interestingFacts: Payment systems should represent states such as pending, authorized, captured, failed, refunded, and disputed explicitly.
Exactly-once delivery across networks is usually approximated with idempotency and deduplication.
Security scope is reduced by tokenizing sensitive payment details.
scenarios.commonInterviewQuestion: Design a payment API that remains safe when a client times out after the provider accepted the charge.

scenarios.title: Instagram Photo Feed
learningObjectives: Separate media upload from feed metadata
Design follower-feed generation and ranking
Use object storage and CDN delivery efficiently

keyDecisions.decision: Why upload media directly to object storage using a controlled URL
keyDecisions.reason: Large payloads bypass application servers while permissions and metadata remain governed.

keyDecisions.decision: Why generate multiple media renditions
keyDecisions.reason: Mobile devices and network conditions differ; serving the appropriate size lowers latency and bandwidth.

keyDecisions.decision: Why use hybrid feed generation
keyDecisions.reason: Precomputation accelerates normal reads, while high-fan-out accounts and ranking may require read-time work.

interestingFacts: Media bytes and social metadata have different storage and caching requirements.
The upload pipeline can process thumbnails, moderation, and metadata asynchronously.
Feed freshness is a product decision as well as a consistency decision.
scenarios.commonInterviewQuestion: How would you design an Instagram feed and media pipeline for users with very different follower counts?

scenarios.title: YouTube Video Platform
learningObjectives: Build an asynchronous upload and transcoding pipeline
Serve global video through edge caching
Design metadata search, recommendations, and view counters separately

keyDecisions.decision: Why transcode uploads asynchronously
keyDecisions.reason: Video encoding is expensive and produces many renditions; it should not block the upload request.

keyDecisions.decision: Why use chunked and resumable upload
keyDecisions.reason: Large uploads frequently lose connectivity. Restarting from zero creates poor user experience and waste.

keyDecisions.decision: Why aggregate view counts asynchronously
keyDecisions.reason: The watch path should not synchronously contend on one hot counter for popular videos.

interestingFacts: Processing and delivery are different planes: upload jobs transform content, while CDN nodes serve segments.
A video may become playable at lower quality before every rendition finishes.
Search indexing is eventually consistent with metadata changes.
scenarios.commonInterviewQuestion: Design YouTube upload, transcoding, and playback for a video that suddenly becomes viral.

scenarios.title: TikTok Short-Video Feed
learningObjectives: Design low-latency personalized feed retrieval
Preload short media efficiently
Capture engagement events for ranking feedback loops

keyDecisions.decision: Why prefetch the next few clips
keyDecisions.reason: Short-form playback creates a narrow time budget; buffering the next likely videos improves continuity.

keyDecisions.decision: Why separate candidate generation from ranking
keyDecisions.reason: A first stage narrows millions of videos; a later stage scores a manageable set using richer features.

keyDecisions.decision: Why stream engagement events asynchronously
keyDecisions.reason: Watch time, skips, likes, and shares feed analytics and models without slowing playback.

interestingFacts: Short-video systems optimize for time-to-first-frame and continuous playback.
Recommendation freshness competes with cacheability.
Safety review and moderation are first-class parts of the publishing pipeline.
scenarios.commonInterviewQuestion: How would you design a personalized short-video feed that starts instantly and learns from user behavior?

scenarios.title: Slack Workspace Messaging
learningObjectives: Design channel history and real-time updates
Support search without overloading the source database
Handle offline clients and workspace isolation

keyDecisions.decision: Why persist channel messages before broadcasting
keyDecisions.reason: A WebSocket broadcast is transient; durable history is the source for reconnect and search indexing.

keyDecisions.decision: Why isolate workspaces logically and operationally
keyDecisions.reason: Tenant boundaries shape authorization, quotas, and blast-radius controls.

keyDecisions.decision: Why index messages asynchronously
keyDecisions.reason: Search should not make the message-send path depend on the search cluster.

interestingFacts: Collaboration platforms combine durable logs with ephemeral presence and typing indicators.
Clients need cursor-based synchronization after reconnect.
Permissions must be applied consistently to search as well as direct history reads.
scenarios.commonInterviewQuestion: Design Slack channels, direct messages, search, and reconnect behavior for a large enterprise workspace.

scenarios.title: Discord Community Chat
learningObjectives: Scale real-time messaging across many servers and channels
Model hot communities separately from ordinary ones
Design message history and gateway sessions

keyDecisions.decision: Why shard gateway connections and channel traffic
keyDecisions.reason: Persistent connections and popular communities create uneven load that cannot be handled by one gateway.

keyDecisions.decision: Why keep message history durable but presence ephemeral
keyDecisions.reason: Messages must survive reconnects; presence can tolerate loss and refresh.

keyDecisions.decision: Why monitor partition hotspots
keyDecisions.reason: One highly active server can dominate a partition even if average traffic looks safe.

interestingFacts: Community chat systems often have highly skewed traffic.
Backpressure is essential when clients or downstream consumers are slow.
Message IDs can help ordering, pagination, and deduplication.
scenarios.commonInterviewQuestion: How would you design Discord for one community that suddenly becomes much hotter than all others?

scenarios.title: Zoom Video Conferencing
learningObjectives: Differentiate signaling from media transport
Reason about latency, regional media relays, and degraded modes
Scale meeting state and recording workflows separately

keyDecisions.decision: Why separate signaling from the media plane
keyDecisions.reason: Joining, permissions, and participant state are control concerns; audio/video packets need low-latency transport.

keyDecisions.decision: Why place media relays near participants
keyDecisions.reason: Interactive communication is sensitive to round-trip latency and packet loss.

keyDecisions.decision: Why process recordings asynchronously
keyDecisions.reason: Recording upload, composition, and transcription are expensive post-meeting workflows.

interestingFacts: Interactive media systems optimize jitter, packet loss, and latency rather than only HTTP request time.
A meeting can degrade video quality while preserving audio.
Regional failover requires careful handling of live session state.
scenarios.commonInterviewQuestion: Design a video-conferencing platform that preserves usable audio during network degradation.

scenarios.title: LinkedIn Professional Network Feed
learningObjectives: Model a relationship graph and feed ranking
Build search and recommendation indexes
Separate write events from derived projections

keyDecisions.decision: Why maintain graph-aware features
keyDecisions.reason: Second-degree connections, mutual relationships, and recommendations depend on relationship traversal.

keyDecisions.decision: Why publish profile changes as events
keyDecisions.reason: Search, feed, notifications, and recommendations can update independently.

keyDecisions.decision: Why apply hybrid feed generation
keyDecisions.reason: Connection graphs and high-fan-out company pages create different cost profiles.

interestingFacts: Professional-network systems combine graph, search, feed, and messaging workloads.
Derived indexes should be rebuildable from durable sources.
Privacy settings must filter every projection, not only profile pages.
scenarios.commonInterviewQuestion: How would you design LinkedIn's people-you-may-know feature and keep it privacy-safe?

scenarios.title: Spotify Music Streaming
learningObjectives: Separate audio delivery from recommendation services
Design playlist and library consistency
Use edge caching and asynchronous analytics

keyDecisions.decision: Why cache audio segments at the edge
keyDecisions.reason: Audio is immutable enough to cache aggressively and should not traverse application services repeatedly.

keyDecisions.decision: Why model playlist updates carefully
keyDecisions.reason: Concurrent edits, ordering, and offline clients require version-aware synchronization.

keyDecisions.decision: Why stream listening events asynchronously
keyDecisions.reason: Recommendations, royalty analytics, and product metrics need events but playback should stay responsive.

interestingFacts: Audio delivery and recommendation ranking have different scaling characteristics.
Offline playback adds entitlement, expiry, and synchronization questions.
Platform tooling matters when many backend services evolve independently.
scenarios.commonInterviewQuestion: Design Spotify playback, playlists, and personalized recommendations for global users.

scenarios.title: GitHub Code Hosting
learningObjectives: Separate Git object storage from web metadata
Design repository events and background jobs
Handle database failover without corrupting writes

keyDecisions.decision: Why separate Git objects from issue and permission metadata
keyDecisions.reason: Repository blobs and commits have content-addressable behavior; product metadata needs transactional queries.

keyDecisions.decision: Why run CI hooks, indexing, and notifications asynchronously
keyDecisions.reason: Repository writes should finish without waiting for every integration.

keyDecisions.decision: Why use careful failover controls for database primaries
keyDecisions.reason: Incorrect promotion during replication problems can create split-brain risk and data divergence.

interestingFacts: Content-addressed objects naturally deduplicate identical content.
Repository events fan out to webhooks, indexing, notifications, and automation.
Operational safeguards around primary promotion are as important as replication itself.
scenarios.commonInterviewQuestion: Design GitHub repository hosting, webhooks, and metadata storage for large organizations.

scenarios.title: Dropbox File Synchronization
learningObjectives: Design chunked uploads and content deduplication
Synchronize file metadata across devices
Handle conflicts and offline edits

keyDecisions.decision: Why upload file chunks rather than whole files
keyDecisions.reason: Chunking supports resumable transfer, deduplication, and partial re-upload after edits.

keyDecisions.decision: Why keep metadata separate from blob content
keyDecisions.reason: Folder structure, versions, sharing, and permissions change independently from stored bytes.

keyDecisions.decision: Why track versions or revisions
keyDecisions.reason: Offline devices may edit the same file; conflicts need deterministic detection and user-visible resolution.

interestingFacts: File synchronization is a metadata-coordination problem as much as a storage problem.
Content hashes can reduce repeated uploads.
Deletion often needs tombstones so offline devices learn that an item was removed.
scenarios.commonInterviewQuestion: Design Dropbox synchronization for large files, offline edits, and cross-device conflict resolution.

scenarios.title: Google Search Engine
learningObjectives: Understand crawl, index, and query-serving separation
Reason about inverted indexes and ranking stages
Build fault-tolerant distributed query fan-out

keyDecisions.decision: Why build an inverted index
keyDecisions.reason: The engine needs to find documents by terms quickly rather than scan every page for each query.

keyDecisions.decision: Why separate offline indexing from online query serving
keyDecisions.reason: Crawling and ranking pipelines are compute-heavy; query serving needs low latency and predictable availability.

keyDecisions.decision: Why use multiple ranking stages
keyDecisions.reason: Cheap retrieval narrows candidates before expensive scoring applies richer signals.

interestingFacts: A search engine is a collection of pipelines, indexes, and query-serving systems rather than one database.
Freshness and quality compete with indexing cost.
Tail latency matters because one slow shard can delay the whole result page.
scenarios.commonInterviewQuestion: Design web search from crawler scheduling through query serving and ranking.

scenarios.title: Gmail Email Platform
learningObjectives: Design durable mailbox storage and thread views
Build search indexing and spam filtering pipelines
Handle send, receive, attachments, and retries

keyDecisions.decision: Why queue outbound delivery
keyDecisions.reason: Remote mail servers can be unavailable; retry schedules and bounce handling should not block the user request.

keyDecisions.decision: Why store attachments separately from mailbox metadata
keyDecisions.reason: Large immutable objects and small mutable message state have different storage and caching needs.

keyDecisions.decision: Why build search indexes asynchronously
keyDecisions.reason: Mailbox operations remain durable even if indexing is briefly delayed.

interestingFacts: Email is a store-and-forward system designed for asynchronous delivery.
Threading is a derived presentation model based on message metadata.
Spam and abuse controls affect deliverability and resource protection.
scenarios.commonInterviewQuestion: Design Gmail send, inbox, search, attachments, threading, and spam-handling paths.

scenarios.title: Redis as a System
learningObjectives: Reason about a low-latency in-memory server
Understand persistence, replication, and cluster partitioning
Identify hot keys, memory pressure, and command-level risks

keyDecisions.decision: Why keep the primary data path in memory
keyDecisions.reason: Avoiding disk seeks enables very low command latency, but memory becomes a deliberate capacity limit.

keyDecisions.decision: Why partition keys across slots or shards
keyDecisions.reason: One server has finite memory and CPU. Partitioning spreads data and request load.

keyDecisions.decision: Why treat command complexity as part of API design
keyDecisions.reason: A single expensive operation over a large collection can block or degrade other requests.

interestingFacts: Redis supports pipelining so clients can reduce round trips.
Redis Cluster uses a defined partitioning model for routing keys across nodes.
Latency investigation should separate server processing from network and operating-system effects.
scenarios.commonInterviewQuestion: How would you design a Redis-like cache with TTLs, eviction, replication, failover, and horizontal partitioning?
